gaps.sentence: I'd prefer ___ at home rather than go out.
gaps.explanation: would prefer + to-infinitive: I'd prefer to eat. (prefer + -ing for general likes.)

gaps.sentence: She can't afford ___ her car repaired this month.
gaps.explanation: afford + to-infinitive: can't afford to get.

gaps.sentence: He's not used to ___ so early.
gaps.explanation: be used TO + -ing: not used to getting (it's a habit he isn't accustomed to).

gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
I tried ___ the shelf up, but it was too heavy.
gaps.explanation: try + to-infinitive = attempt, make an effort.

gaps.sentence: Do you have any idea how ___ this knot?
gaps.explanation: question word + to-infinitive: how to undo.

gaps.sentence: He denied ___ the money, but nobody believed him.
The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.
